context.heading: 10.2.1. Reset Gate and Update Gate
context.before: Here, the LSTM’s three gates are replaced by two: the reset gate and the update gate. As with LSTMs, these gates are given sigmoid activations, forcing their values to lie in the interval \((0, 1)\). Intuitively, the reset gate controls how much of the previous state we might still want to remember. Likewise, an update gate would allow us to control how much of the new state is just a copy of the old one. Fig. 10.2.1 illustrates the inputs for both the reset and update gates in a GRU, given the input of the current time step and the hidden state of the previous time step. The outputs of the gates are given by two fully connected layers with a sigmoid activation function.
context.after: Mathematically, for a given time step \(t\), suppose that the input is a minibatch \(\mathbf{X}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}\) (number of examples \(=n\); number of inputs \(=d\)) and the hidden state of the previous time step is \(\mathbf{H}_{t-1} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times h}\) (number of hidden units \(=h\)). context.heading: 10.2.2. Candidate Hidden State
context.before: Fig. 10.2.2 illustrates the computational flow after applying the reset gate.
context.after: Finally, we need to incorporate the effect of the update gate \(\mathbf{Z}_t\). This determines the extent to which the new hidden state \(\mathbf{H}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times h}\) matches the old state \(\mathbf{H}_{t-1}\) compared with how much it resembles the new candidate state \(\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_t\). The update gate \(\mathbf{Z}_t\) can be used for this purpose, simply by taking elementwise convex combinations of \(\mathbf{H}_{t-1}\) and \(\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_t\). context.before: Whenever the update gate \(\mathbf{Z}_t\) is close to 1, we simply retain the old state. In this case the information from \(\mathbf{X}_t\) is ignored, effectively skipping time step \(t\) in the dependency chain. By contrast, whenever \(\mathbf{Z}_t\) is close to 0, the new latent state \(\mathbf{H}_t\) approaches the candidate latent state \(\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_t\).
